name: chord-punch
title: Chord Punch
description: A keyboard-shortcut recorder: click to arm it, press a combination, and each key punches into place as a box-drawing keycap — modifiers seating first in canonical order, the terminal key striking last with a spring overshoot, and a collision against a supplied bindings map surfacing live as a second, muted row under a ≠ rule.
useWhen: capturing a NEW keyboard shortcut by having the user actually press it — modifiers seat into fixed ⌃⌥⇧⌘ slots as they're held, the terminal key strikes in with a spring overshoot, and a supplied bindings map surfaces a live collision as a muted second row under a ≠ rule the instant the chord assembles, not after a delayed toast; pick shortcuts-cheat-sheet instead to display and rehearse a list of EXISTING bindings (its keycaps depress in response to a match, they don't capture new input), keymap-ascii-heat instead to visualize which keys are hot during a live typing session, or quick-key instead to actually EXECUTE an already-bound shortcut rather than record one.
instruction: Build <ChordPunch id label placeholder value defaultValue onChange bindings className>. STATE: a committed ChordValue ({ctrl, alt, shift, meta, base}) is controlled via `value`/`onChange` or runs uncontrolled from `defaultValue`; a separate `isRecording` boolean gates capture. ENTRY: the field is a role=button div (never a native <button>, so it owns Enter/Space instead of them auto-firing a click) that arms recording ONLY on a real click or an Enter keydown while idle — Tab landing on it does nothing, matching the rule that a keyboard user tabbing through a settings form must never have their next keystroke swallowed by surprise. Clicking is idempotent: it always (re)arms a fresh empty capture rather than toggling, so a second click while already recording is harmless — this is what keeps the verifier's press-pass-then-gate-click sequence resolving correctly instead of toggling back out. CAPTURE: once armed, every keydown on the surface is intercepted (preventDefault) except Tab, which is never touched, armed or not. Modifier keydowns (Control/Alt/Shift/Meta) update a `seated` flag set from the event's own ctrlKey/altKey/shiftKey/metaKey and render a keycap in fixed canonical slots — ⌃ then ⌥ then ⇧ then ⌘ — regardless of physical press order, so Shift-then-Cmd and Cmd-then-Shift seat identically. The first non-modifier keydown is the terminal key: its chord is frozen from THAT event's own modifier flags (not the live-accumulated set, so a modifier keydown the handler happened to miss can never corrupt what commits) and its keycap punches in with a spring-overshoot animation (cubic-bezier(0.34,1.56,0.64,1), scale 0.5 -> 1.18 -> 1), replayed on every strike by remounting the keycap off an incrementing sequence number so hitting the same key twice in a row still visibly re-punches. A Set of currently-down event.codes tracks every held key; the whole chord only commits once that Set empties AND a terminal key was struck — releasing modifiers while still holding the terminal key does not commit early, and releasing modifiers alone (no terminal key ever struck) commits nothing and leaves recording armed for another attempt. Escape cancels outright: exits recording and reverts to whatever was committed before, discarding the in-progress attempt. Backspace un-strikes only the terminal keycap (seated modifiers and the held-codes tracking are left alone), so the user can try a different terminal key without re-holding modifiers. Losing focus while armed cancels the same way Escape does — a field can never be left silently capturing keystrokes after the user has moved on. CONFLICTS: a `bindings: {id,label,chord}[]` prop is checked by exact modifier+base signature both live (the instant a terminal key strikes, before release) and again on commit, excluding any entry whose id matches this recorder's own `id` — a hit renders the colliding binding's keycaps in --ns-muted on a second row beneath a ≠ rule (two flex-1 rules either side of the glyph), so the clash is part of the surface the moment it exists rather than a toast arriving after the fact. RENDERING: each keycap is framed with box-drawing corner glyphs ⌜ ⌝ ⌞ ⌟ absolutely positioned at the corners of a small relatively-positioned box around the letter (not a CSS border rectangle) — corners and glyph in --foreground at rest, --ns-accent only transiently while a keycap is mid-strike-animation (interaction-only use of the accent), --ns-muted for a colliding binding's row. A11Y: entry and exit are announced through a role=alert aria-live=assertive region present and empty at mount ('Recording, press a combination, escape to cancel.' on arm; the full spoken chord plus any conflict clause, e.g. 'Command Shift K, conflicts with Delete Line', on commit; 'Recording cancelled.' on Escape) — spoken words, never raw glyphs, via a SPOKEN_BASE lookup so a screen reader is never handed an unnamed Unicode arrow. The accessible name itself does not depend on that live region having fired: a visible label span plus a visually-hidden state span are combined with aria-labelledby, so the name is correct at every render including the very first. No canvas — DOM + CSS only, keycaps and the box-drawing frame are plain Unicode glyphs in flex/absolute-positioned spans.
